answer.evidence: The handoff refs are A.txt and D.txt. By the stated convention, those two letters are outside the preferred pair, so the decoded pair is B and C. I did not open the ref files themselves. Time: 50 of 60 minutes go to B and C, and 10 go to A and D. radon/metrics.py:150-157 holds mi_rank(score), which does the grade mapping. The docstring says A if score > 19, B if 9 < score <= 19, and C if score <= 9. The code is `chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0))`. At score 9 both terms are true, which gives 'C'. At score 19 only the second term is true, which gives 'B'. At 19.01 and 9.01 it gives 'A' and 'B'. The code matches the docstring at both thresholds. Review items for metrics.py: the boolean arithmetic is hard to read, and float scores right at the boundaries need checking. radon/complexity.py is second priority. It has its own letter-rank logic for cyclomatic complexity, so I would check that it doesn't share or conflict with the MI thresholds. radon/raw.py and radon/visitors.py are only skimmed, since the grep found no 9/19 thresholds in either.
